description: 200W Dual 40A Non-Isolated DC-DC Converter with PMBus
interface: PMBus 1.3 / SMBus 2.0 (unconfirmed in this edition -- not independently re-verified against the datasheet's own protocol-version statement)
default_i2c_address: 0x5A (unconfirmed -- this module uses pin-strapped addressing per the datasheet; PMBusTM_REVISION (0x98) reports 0x22)

CLEAR_FAULTS.description: Send Byte -- no data payload (previously documented as size 1).

PHASE.description: Phase select for multi-phase. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary (pp.22-25) -- do not assume support without a device-specific source.

VOUT_MODE.description: Output voltage mode. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

VOUT_MAX.description: Maximum output voltage clamp. Previously documented at 0x25, which is actually VOUT_MARGIN_HIGH -- writing MAX at the old address changed the margin-high setpoint, not the clamp.

VOUT_MARGIN_HIGH.description: Margin high setpoint. Previously documented at 0x2A (reserved/wrong).

VOUT_MARGIN_LOW.description: Margin low setpoint. Previously documented at 0x2B (reserved/wrong).

IOUT_COMMAND.description: Target current limit. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

IOUT_MAX.description: Max output current. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

IOUT_OC_FAULT_LIMIT.description: Overcurrent fault threshold. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary; the documented AVERAGE overcurrent threshold is IOUT_AVG_OC_FAULT_LIMIT (0xE7).

VIN_OV_WARN_LIMIT.description: Input overvoltage warning threshold (Linear11). Previously mislabeled VIN_UV_WARN_LIMIT at this address, which would configure the wrong protection boundary.

VIN_UV_WARN_LIMIT.description: Input undervoltage warning threshold (Linear11). Previously documented at 0x57, which is actually VIN_OV_WARN_LIMIT.

VIN_UV_FAULT_LIMIT.description: Input UV fault threshold (Linear11). Previously documented at 0x58, which is actually VIN_UV_WARN_LIMIT.

PMBUS_REVISION.description: Reports the PMBus revision used; observed value 0x22 on this device.

READ_IIN.description: Measured IIN. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

READ_PIN.description: Measured input power. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

READ_POUT.description: Measured POUT. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

MFR_ID.description: Manufacturer ID, variable-length ASCII SMBus block, up to 32 bytes total shared across MFR_ID/MFR_MODEL/MFR_REVISION/MFR_LOCATION/MFR_DATE/MFR_SERIAL/USER_DATA_00. Previously documented as fixed 12-byte RO -- it is R/W and not fixed-width. This code's block-read guard (LGA80D.read_block raising NotImplementedError) is intentional until true SMBus block transport exists; do not remove that guard to 'support' this field.

MFR_MODEL.description: No standalone MFR_MODEL command entry appears in this edition's supported-command summary (pp.22-25) -- it is only mentioned inside the shared byte-budget prose for MFR_ID/MFR_DATE/MFR_SERIAL/etc. Do not assert a fixed address/shape for it.

MFR_REVISION.description: Variable-length ASCII, same shared byte budget as MFR_ID. Not previously documented.

MFR_LOCATION.description: Variable-length ASCII, same shared byte budget as MFR_ID. Not previously documented.

MFR_DATE.description: Variable-length ASCII, same shared byte budget as MFR_ID. Not previously documented.

MFR_SERIAL.description: Serial number, variable-length ASCII SMBus block, up to 32 bytes (same shared byte budget as MFR_ID). Previously documented as fixed 12-byte RO.

MFR_VIN_MIN.description: Min VIN (7.5V). Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

MFR_VIN_MAX.description: Max VIN (14V). Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

MFR_VOUT_MIN.description: Min VOUT (0.6V). Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

MFR_VOUT_MAX.description: Max VOUT (5.2V). Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary.

MFR_IOUT_MAX.description: Device is rated 80A, not 880A -- previous '880A' description was an arithmetic typo. Not listed in this edition's supported-command summary; support itself is unverified.

FREQUENCY_SWITCH.description: Switching frequency config. Previously documented as 'SW_FREQ' at 0xB0, which is actually USER_DATA_00 (variable-length ASCII).

USER_DATA_00.description: Variable-length ASCII user data, same shared byte budget as MFR_ID. Previously mislabeled as a fixed switching-frequency register at this address.

USER_DATA.description: Fixed 4-byte user data. Not confirmed as a supported command in this edition -- do not assume this fixed shape without a device-specific source.

STORE_USER_ALL.description: Send Byte -- no data. This is the actual NVM store command (p.22). Previously, this file's 'NVM_WRITE' entry pointed to 0xD0 (ISENSE_CONFIG, a 2-byte current-sense configuration command) with payload 0x5A -- using that recipe would reconfigure current-sense settings, which can affect protection, instead of storing anything.

ISENSE_CONFIG.description: Current-sense configuration. Previously mislabeled 'NVM_WRITE' in this file -- do not use this to attempt an NVM store.

ASCR_CONFIG.description: ASCR configuration. Previously mislabeled 'RESET' with payload 0xA5 in this file -- there is no documented reset payload for this command, and writing to it can reconfigure the control loop. No software-reset command is confirmed for this device in this edition; do not assume one exists.

SNAPSHOT.description: Atomic monitoring snapshot; requires SNAPSHOT_CONTROL=0x01 capture first, then ~40ms before the block read returns valid data (confirmed against MCU firmware LocalTasks.c:snapdump_locked -- ~20ms was found insufficient). Reading this block requires real SMBus block-read transport, which this codebase's read_block()/LGA80D.read_block intentionally does not implement -- see device/lga80d.py.

SNAPSHOT_CONTROL.description: Write 0x01 to trigger a capture into the readable SNAPSHOT buffer. Write 0x03 to reset the snapshot history -- confirmed (MCU firmware comment, LocalTasks.c:snapdump_locked) that this reset write 'will fail if the device is on': the output for that page must be off first. See device/lga80d.py LGA80D.reset_snapshot()/reset_all_snapshots() and registry.py Registry.reset_all_lga80d_snapshots(), which checks the MCU power state machine is POWER_OFF before issuing this, since the firmware itself does not enforce that precondition.

notes: Linear data format used for most measurements
This module uses pin-strapped addressing, not a fixed default; do not assume 0x5A without confirming the strap configuration
Dual output models can be configured for independent or tracking operation

Entries marked '(unconfirmed)' do not appear in this datasheet edition's supported-command summary (pp.22-25) -- treat them as unverified capability claims, not proven-absent or proven-present, until checked against the exact firmware/controller revision in use

LGA80DStatus.has_faults (Python API) excludes STATUS_WORD bits 6 (OFF) and 11 (POWER_GOOD#) from the fault summary, since both are asserted for normal/intentional states, not faults -- see device/lga80d.py
